name: Ushabti
body:
Ushabti
CR 6

XP 2,400
LN Medium construct (extraplanar, lawful)
Init +1 Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +5

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 11, flat-footed 17 (+2 deflection, +1 Dex, +5 natural)
hp 74 (8d10+30)
Fort +4, Ref +5, Will +11
Immune construct immunities (see weaknesses, below)
Weaknesses ensouled

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee +11/+6 disrupting light mace (1d6+3 bludgeoning plus disruption Will DC 14 negates, 20/x2)
Spellcasting (CL 5th concentration +14)

The Ushabti casts spells as a 5th-level cleric.

3rd–bestow curse (Will DC 18), elemental speech, wrathful mantle
2nd–align weapon, consecrate, ghostbane dirge, weapon of awe (prepared twice)
1st–bane, cause fear (prepared twice) (Will DC 16), command (prepared twice) (Will DC 16)
0th–create water, guidance, light, mending, purify food and drink, read magic, virtue

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 13, Con –, Int 12, Wis 21, Cha 15
Base Atk +8; CMB +10; CMD 21
Feats Combat Casting, Combat Expertise, Craft Magic Arms and Armor, Iron Will
Skills Craft (any one) +9, Knowledge (planes, religion) +9
Languages Common, Celestial
Gear ring of protection +2, jeweled pectoral of resistance +2 (as cloak), +1 disrupting light mace

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Ensouled (Ex)

Ushabti have a soul and unlike other constructs, and as such, is affected by mind-affecting effects normally, lacking the normal construct immunity.

Masterfully Made (Ex)

Ushabti gain bonus hp as if it were a Large construct.

ECOLOGY

Environment any (extraplanar)
Organization solitary, or found in groups approximating social groupings found in life
Treasure double standard (in lair and including combat gear)

Ushabti are masterfully constructed, life-size statues of a deceased noble hewn from rich stone quarried at enormous expense. These statues are dressed in fine linen, gold and jewels, suitable to the deceased’s station. Buried with the deceased they were commissioned for, ushabti were enchanted to awaken to life in the next world, and perform any labor the dead soul would be called upon to undertake in the afterlife.

Ushabti are common among the myriad planes of the afterlife, where they labor endlessly, or work to directly protect the deceased soul that commissioned them.

Ushabti are intelligent, dispassionate and hardworking, with strong and disciplined minds. Ushabti are higher in the social order than shabti, and share a similar origin. Ushabti often command vast troops of their lesser kin, acting as overseers of the enormous slave-gangs that toil tirelessly to build the logistical foundations of heaven.
